task.description:
Step 0.5 + Step 1 combined (WF-03_issue_resolving.md). This is Step 0.5 (registry lookup) + Step 1 (diagnose) for ISS-0459. Do NOT trust ISS-0459.yaml's filing prose as settled fact -- re-derive independently per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md section 1.1: a handoff/record's factual claims are checkable and may be wrong.

STEP 0.5: search docs/issues/ for a prior resolved entry covering this exact gap (a release_lock status for a terminal-but-not-resolved WF-03 outcome). Report whether a match exists.

STEP 1 -- re-derive the diagnosis from the actual source, not from the filing:
1. Open letflow-queue's OWN source (paths in artifacts_in above, in the sibling checkout c:/Users/tvolo/dev/ai-dala/letflow-queue) and confirm, first-hand, what release_lock's actual legal status values are and what get_next_task's actual SQL eligibility predicate is. Quote the exact code.
2. Specifically verify or refute this candidate finding, stated here as a claim to check, not as settled: letflow_queue/tasks/task.ex line 18 defines @statuses ~w(open done blocked) -- i.e. 'blocked' is ALREADY a legal release_lock status today, and tasks.ex's get_next_task/1 SQL eligibility predicate filters on t.status = 'open' only, meaning a task released with status:blocked is ALREADY excluded from future get_next_task claims. Also verify: tap_maybe_close_github_issue/2 only fires on status == "done" (see tasks.ex ~line 382-399), so releasing with status:blocked does NOT best-effort-close the GitHub issue. If both of these check out, the LIFO re-selection HAZARD described in ISS-0459 may already be preventable today by releasing with status:"blocked" instead of status:"done" or no-status -- state plainly whether this is true, and if so, why TASK_QUEUE.md's own text (as quoted in ISS-0459's own description, and as you should re-read directly) does not already document this as the answer. Consider: does 'blocked' as an English word semantically mismatched the instrumented/no_defect meaning badly enough that documenting it under that name would misinform a future reader, even if it is mechanically sufficient? Give your own reasoned judgment, do not just report symptom.
3. State plainly: does ANY existing letflow-queue status value, or ANY existing TASK_QUEUE.md-documented mechanism, already fully satisfy ISS-0459's Acceptance Criterion 1 (a release_lock status/mechanism that marks a task terminally closed for LIFO-selection purposes without asserting resolved and without best-effort-closing an already-closed GitHub issue)? Your answer drives whether CODE-DESIGNER's next step is 'add a new status value + migration' or 'document existing blocked semantics correctly, no code change' or something else.
4. Do NOT implement anything. Do NOT edit letflow-queue's source. Do NOT edit TASK_QUEUE.md or ISSUE_QUEUE.md yet -- that is CODE-DESIGNER's and then ELIXIR-DEV's job, after a design gate.
5. Write your diagnosis into result.summary: root cause (confirmed or refuted against source), the 'blocked' finding's verdict, and what a fix needs to change (or confirm needs no code change, only docs).
acceptance_criteria: Step 0.5: docs/issues/ searched for a prior resolved match; result stated explicitly (found/not found)
letflow-queue source code quoted first-hand (not inferred from README prose alone) for: @statuses, get_next_task's SQL WHERE clause, and tap_maybe_close_github_issue's guard clause
The 'blocked already solves this' candidate finding is explicitly confirmed or refuted with the quoted evidence
A clear statement of what CODE-DESIGNER needs to design: new status value vs. documentation-only vs. other
No implementation, no file edits outside this handoff

result.summary:
STEP 0.5 (registry lookup): grepped docs/issues/ for LIFO|release_lock.*status|blocked.*status|re-selection|reclaim.*task (case-insensitive) across all 225 files. 12 matches, none is a resolved entry covering this exact gap (a release_lock status for a terminal-but-not-resolved WF-03 outcome) -- they are unrelated prior uses of the word 'blocked' (ISS-0108/0109/0106/0071 concern the auto-close-on-done incident this file's own TASK_QUEUE.md section already narrates; ISS-0277/0278/0285 concern that same incident's follow-up; ISS-0225/0230/0296/0388 are unrelated). NO PRIOR MATCH FOUND. This is a first occurrence, not a recurrence -- severity stays as filed (MINOR), no upgrade per WF-03 Step 0.5's recurrence rule.

STEP 1 (diagnose), re-derived from letflow-queue source directly, not from ISS-0459's filing prose or from TASK_QUEUE.md's prose alone:

1) @statuses -- letflow-queue/lib/letflow_queue/tasks/task.ex:18: `@statuses ~w(open done blocked)`. CONFIRMED: 'blocked' is already a legal Task status value today. (Note: this module attribute is not actually referenced by any changeset's validate_inclusion(:status, ...) -- release_lock/2's own status legality check lives separately in tasks.ex:351, `status not in [nil, "open", "done", "blocked"] -> {:error, :invalid_status}` -- same three-value vocabulary, independently confirmed.)

2) get_next_task/1 SQL eligibility predicate -- letflow-queue/lib/letflow_queue/tasks.ex:171-209. Both the issue-type and requirement-type candidate subqueries filter `WHERE t.status = 'open' AND t.locked_by IS NULL AND ...`. CONFIRMED: a task whose status is 'blocked' (or 'done') can never satisfy either subquery's WHERE clause, so it is permanently ineligible for claim by get_next_task -- there is no code path back to 'open' status other than a future release_lock/set_lock call explicitly writing it. This directly refutes the LIFO re-selection hazard for a task released with status:blocked: the exact SQL that produced ISS-0459's observed hazard (task 458 re-claimed twice after a no-status release left it status='open') cannot fire against a status='blocked' row.

3) tap_maybe_close_github_issue/2 -- letflow-queue/lib/letflow_queue/tasks.ex:382-401. The function clause that actually closes the GitHub issue pattern-matches `{:ok, %Task{status: "done", ...}}, "done"` (both the task's post-update status AND the status argument must literally be "done"); the fallback clause `tap_maybe_close_github_issue(result, _status), do: result` is a pure passthrough for every other status, including "blocked". CONFIRMED: releasing with status:"blocked" does NOT best-effort-close the linked GitHub issue -- no GitHub.close_issue/1 call occurs on that path at all.

4) Test-suite corroboration (not requested by the task but strengthens confidence past reading the source alone): letflow-queue/test/letflow_queue/tasks_test.exs:109 asserts get_next_task 'does not return a task that is already done or blocked'; :312-319 and :344-345 assert release_lock(status: "blocked") both succeeds and is force-releasable. This is shipped, tested behavior, not a code path that merely happens to work today and could silently regress.

VERDICT ON THE 'BLOCKED ALREADY SOLVES THIS' CANDIDATE FINDING: CONFIRMED, mechanically. Releasing queue task 458 (or any future instrumented/no_defect-terminal task) with release_lock(status:"blocked") instead of status:"done" or no-status would have: (a) permanently excluded it from get_next_task's eligibility predicate -- no LIFO re-selection loop -- while (b) NOT asserting the underlying defect is resolved at the queue-status-word level, and (c) NOT triggering a best-effort close of an already-closed GitHub issue (a harmless no-op either way, since GitHub itself is idempotent on re-closing, but 'blocked' skips even attempting it, which is arguably cleaner than 'done's redundant close call). All three of ISS-0459's implied requirements are mechanically satisfiable today with zero code change.

WHY TASK_QUEUE.md DOESN'T ALREADY DOCUMENT THIS AS THE ANSWER: read TASK_QUEUE.md in full (this handoff's owned_modules). Its only three mentions of 'blocked' are: line 167 ('report blocked, do not select' -- an unrelated ORCH-reachability sense of the English word, not the queue status), line 300 (a stage-activity definition inside the deferral-staleness section, again unrelated -- it's talking about docs/requirements.yaml status values, a different vocabulary from the queue's own Task.status), and line 471 ('the queue's own status field (open/done/blocked)') plus line 476, both of which only *name* blocked as one of the three legal enum values in passing, inside a paragraph about docs/requirements.yaml being a mirror -- neither explains what 'blocked' means, when to use it, or that it is the mechanism for closing out a WF-03 instrumented/no_defect run. Section '4. release_lock' (lines 394-441), which is where a reader would look for exactly this answer, documents only two cases in detail: status:"done" (with a full paragraph on the done-vs-finished-cleanly distinction, correctly warning against conflating them) and no-status (open, full hand-back). 'blocked' is never mentioned in that section at all, despite being one of only three legal values release_lock accepts. So the gap is real: the mechanism exists and works, but is undocumented at the one place TASK_QUEUE.md's own structure would lead a reader to look for it, and ISS-0459's filing agent (and this run, independently, before checking source) both had no way to discover it from the docs alone.

REASONED JUDGMENT ON THE SEMANTIC MISMATCH (asked for explicitly, not just the mechanical answer): 'blocked' as an English word is a bad name for this meaning, badly enough that documenting today's status value under its current bare name would misinform a future reader even though it is mechanically correct. 'Blocked' overwhelmingly reads, to any agent or human skimming queue state, as 'stuck, waiting on something, still needs action' (see this project's OWN other uses of the word: docs/agents/protocols/TASK_QUEUE.md:311's 'blocked-by:' deferral prefix, and the ordinary English sense ORCH itself uses at TASK_QUEUE.md:167, 'report blocked'). Every one of those senses implies the task is NOT done, is actionable, and should be revisited -- which is the OPPOSITE of what ISS-0459's use case needs to communicate (a task that was investigated to a genuine, stable, terminal stopping point -- instrumented or no_defect -- and should NOT be revisited by that path again). A future ORCH session or human skimming `status='blocked'` in the queue, or in a status report, would reasonably conclude 'this needs to be unblocked and worked,' exactly backwards from 'this was already fully investigated and correctly is not being worked further.' Reusing the bare word without a documented, explicit convention is a foot-gun: two different future writers could use 'blocked' for two different intents (a genuinely stuck/actionable task vs. an instrumented/no_defect terminal one) and nothing in the schema disambiguates them -- the queue's Task schema carries no sub-reason field, only the bare three-value status. So: mechanically sufficient today, semantically unsafe to ship as an undocumented convention.

WHAT SATISFIES ISS-0459's ACCEPTANCE CRITERION 1 TODAY: the existing 'blocked' status value and existing release_lock(status:"blocked") mechanism, used exactly as-is with NO letflow-queue code change and NO migration. What is genuinely missing is DOCUMENTATION -- specifically, TASK_QUEUE.md's release_lock section needs an explicit third case (alongside 'done' and no-status) stating: when a WF-03 run's Step 5 reaches a terminal-but-not-resolved outcome (instrumented or no_defect, per ISSUE_QUEUE.md's status vocabulary), ORCH releases with status:"blocked" -- naming the precise trigger condition, cross-referencing ISSUE_QUEUE.md's instrumented/no_defect definitions so the two documents' vocabularies are tied together explicitly (they are not today), and ideally noting the semantic-mismatch risk above so a future reader understands why this named value was chosen over inventing a new one, and doesn't casually reuse plain 'blocked' releases for an actually-stuck/actionable task without distinguishing the two in the release comment or a future task field.

WHAT CODE-DESIGNER NEEDS TO DESIGN: documentation-only. No new letflow-queue status value, no migration, no application code change to lib/letflow_queue/. The design artefact should specify: (a) the exact new prose to add to TASK_QUEUE.md's section 4 (release_lock) describing the instrumented/no_defect -> status:"blocked" convention, its trigger condition, and its cross-reference to ISSUE_QUEUE.md's status vocabulary; (b) whether ISSUE_QUEUE.md's own Step 5 / status-vocabulary section needs a parallel cross-reference back (so a reader landing there first also learns the queue-side consequence); (c) a decision on the semantic-mismatch concern above -- CODE-DESIGNER should decide, and state a reasoned position, on whether to accept 'blocked' as-is (cheapest, ships today) or recommend a follow-on letflow-queue enhancement (e.g. a fourth status value or a status-reason sub-field) as a SEPARATE, filed issue rather than blocking this documentation fix on a queue-service code change; (d) confirm no change to docs/agents/workflows/WF-03_issue_resolving.md's Step 5 prose is needed beyond what it already says (it currently doesn't mention release_lock status at all in its own text -- the release_lock trigger is documented only in TASK_QUEUE.md today -- CODE-DESIGNER should decide if WF-03 Step 5 also needs an explicit pointer). This run made NO changes to TASK_QUEUE.md, ISSUE_QUEUE.md, or any letflow-queue source file -- diagnosis only, per the handoff's task.description and per WF-03's Step 1 boundary.
result.next_action: Route to CODE-DESIGNER for fix design (documentation-only: TASK_QUEUE.md section 4 release_lock, plus possibly ISSUE_QUEUE.md cross-reference and WF-03_issue_resolving.md Step 5 pointer -- specify the instrumented/no_defect -> release_lock(status:"blocked") convention and its trigger condition; CODE-DESIGNER should also decide whether to recommend a separate follow-on issue proposing a less semantically-overloaded queue status/reason field, rather than blocking this doc fix on a letflow-queue code change).
